claims.text: Atomically dispersed platinum on ceria-zirconia will improve catalytic activity relative to conventional platinum nanoparticles on alumina.
Atomically dispersed platinum on ceria-zirconia will improve catalyst durability relative to conventional platinum nanoparticles on alumina.
The proposed catalyst will permit lower overall platinum loading than conventional platinum nanoparticles on alumina.
Atomic layer deposition can facilitate single-atom platinum dispersion on ceria-zirconia.
The ceria-zirconia support stabilizes atomically dispersed platinum sites.
Atomically dispersed platinum on ceria-zirconia provides a high density of interfacial active sites.
Stabilization of atomically dispersed platinum by ceria-zirconia prevents or retards platinum sintering.
Enhanced interaction between atomically dispersed platinum and ceria-zirconia increases oxygen storage at the catalyst surface.
Enhanced interaction between atomically dispersed platinum and ceria-zirconia increases oxygen activation at the catalyst surface.
Improved metal-support synergy facilitates oxygen delivery to reactants.
Improved oxygen delivery boosts catalytic efficiency.
Retarded platinum sintering improves catalyst durability.
The atomically dispersed platinum/ceria-zirconia catalyst will have a lower light-off temperature than the platinum-nanoparticle/alumina baseline.
The atomically dispersed platinum/ceria-zirconia catalyst will degrade more slowly than the platinum-nanoparticle/alumina baseline.
The expected benefits should persist over multiple thermal cycles in typical simulated exhaust gas compositions.
